text:
oncall-alex: I just saw a spike of failed decrypts from service-account:batch-ingest-sa at 02:14 UTC, alerted by monitoring. Investigating now.
sec-jen: copying — can you paste the metric link and recent logs?
oncall-alex: https://infra.redwood.internal/alerts/alert-8851 metric shows 1.2k decrypt_errors/min, started ~02:12.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-317, severity:high. PagerDuty notified.
sre-pat: tagging logs: running `gcloud logging read 'resource.type="k8s_container" AND jsonPayload.message:"decrypt"' --limit 50` and pulling recent entries.
infra-mig: I'll check KMS key usage, possible unauthorized keyring access. Running `gcloud kms keys versions list --location=us-central1 --keyring=prod-kms --key=ingest-key` now.
oncall-alex: I want quick containment: remove batch-ingest-sa's ability to call KMS decrypt until we understand blast radius.
sec-jen: Agree. Patch RBAC: revoke roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter from batch-ingest-sa on key resource scope. `gcloud projects remove-iam-policy-binding redwood-prod --member=serviceAccount:batch-ingest-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` (previewing).
sre-pat: Before revocation, capture audit trail for last 48 hrs for that SA: `gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail="batch-ingest-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com" AND protoPayload.methodName:"Decrypt"' --limit 1000 --freshness=48h`
oncall-alex: Do that now, paste results.
infra-mig: Pulled logs. Most decrypt calls are from k8s-worker-12 pod batch-worker, couple from eu-west-1 region unexpected. Pasting sample: ```json
{ "timestamp":"2026-03-20T02:13:04Z", "principal":"batch-ingest-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com", "method":"google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt", "resource":"projects/redwood-prod/locations/us-central1/keyRings/prod-kms/cryptoKeys/ingest-key" }
```
sec-jen: EU calls are suspicious. Who deployed anything to eu-west overnight?
eng-lead-maya: No scheduled deploys for batch-ingest to EU. I see a config drift PR open from infra-mig but not merged.
infra-mig: PR not merged, so cannot be a legit deploy. Could be compromised SA used from a different region.
sre-pat: I've revoked the short-lived token on the batch-worker pod and restarted the pod to clear cached tokens. Confirming with restart logs.
oncall-alex: Good. Next: rotate the KMS key's primary version to force new ciphertexts and cut off any re-use. Possible downtime for decryption — is batch ingest tolerant?
eng-lead-maya: Batch ingest can backfill; prefer security. Proceed with rotation and inform downstream teams.
sec-jen: Steps: 1) snapshot audit logs (done) 2) revoke SA decrypt role (will do) 3) rotate KMS key 4) run integrity checks on snapshots.
infra-mig: Starting role removal now. Command executed, awaiting IAM delta propagation (~30s).
ops-bot: IAM binding change detected: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter removed from serviceAccount:batch-ingest-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com.
sec-jen: Confirm no new decrypt calls after revocation.
sre-pat: Monitoring — decrypt call rate dropped to baseline in us-central1, eu calls persisted for ~20s then stopped. Looks contained.
oncall-alex: Now rotating key: `gcloud kms keys versions create --key=ingest-key --keyring=prod-kms --location=us-central1` then set primary to new version. Doing it.
infra-mig: New version created v5, promoting to primary.
ops-bot: KMS key primary version changed: ingest-key v5.
sec-jen: Great. Next: ensure no exported key material, check KMS access audit for AdminCreate or Import operations.
infra-mig: No import/create operations in last 90 days. Only decrypts and encrypts.
sec-jen: Good. Prepare short incident timeline note for postmortem: include initial detection, regions affected, containment actions, IAM revocation, key rotation, pod restarts.
oncall-alex: I'll draft timeline in thread. 02:12 Alert -> 02:13 Investigate logs -> 02:15 Revoke SA decrypt role -> 02:17 Pod restarts -> 02:20 KMS rotation -> 02:22 Containment verified.
eng-lead-maya: Assign follow-ups: (a) rotate any cached secrets in downstream services, (b) run full RBAC sweep for other SAs with decrypt perms, (c) add geo-restriction for batch-ingest SA if possible.
sec-jen: I'll own (b) and (c). sec-jen -> open ticket SECU-2026-88 for RBAC sweep and geo-fencing.
oncall-alex: I'll own (a) and coordinate with data-team on re-encryption/backfill.
sre-pat: Also recommend adding an automated alarm for cross-region decrypts for high-sensitivity keys. I'll put that as SECU-2026-89.
oncall-alex: Need to hand off incident control to next on-call, @oncall-taylor you're up for the 08:00 UTC shift — please pick this up for postmortem and comms.
oncall-taylor: Acknowledged, will take lead. Please drop any outstanding artifacts (log export links, IAM diffs, KMS activity CSV) into INC-2026-317.
infra-mig: Uploading logs and IAM diff to the incident ticket now: https://infra.redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-317/attachments
sec-jen: Postmortem checklist: timeline, root cause hypotheses (compromised SA key vs misconfigured multi-region job), detection gaps, and remediation (RBAC least privilege, KMS usage guardrails, alerting).
oncall-taylor: I'll run the postmortem template and set a sync with stakeholders tomorrow 10:00 UTC.
oncall-alex: Closing incident channel once oncall-taylor confirms handoff. Great work all. :thumbsup:
pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-2026-317 status updated: monitoring -> triaged -> contained.
oncall-taylor: Confirmed pickup, reassigning incident lead to oncall-taylor. Leaving brief notes on actions taken in ticket.
sec-jen: Will schedule a quick review with infra-mig and eng-lead-maya to validate geo restrictions and RBAC policy.
eng-lead-maya: Thanks team. We'll follow up on oncall-taylor's postmortem and track SECU-2026-88/89.
oncall-taylor: Acknowledge. Handoff complete.
